answer: An agent anchors its identity by locking 64 GB of unswappable RAM into a marble array, committing a Blake3 hash to the current epoch root. Verifiers then sweep the cluster with an audit gale, sending a whisper probe targeting pseudo-random memory indices. The agent computes the leaf proof inside an eight-millisecond roundtrip to verify physical presence. A timeout or hash mismatch immediately slashes 1500 tokens and purges the seat, raising attack cost strictly linearly per gigabyte.
